newsitem.title: CHINA: China sugar prices sluggish despite season end.
newsitem.headline: China sugar prices sluggish despite season end.

text.p: China's domestic sugar prices showed no sign of recovery despite the approach of the end of the crushing season, officials said on Monday.
"Currently, sugar prices are fairly sluggish," an official of the China Sugar and Wine Co (Group) said. "Stockpiles are still at high levels."
Domestic sugar prices dipped when the 1996/97 crushing season (October/April) began last October.
Wholesale sugar prices in the capital Beijing are now about 4,100 yuan ($494) per tonne, the official said, compared with about 4,300 yuan in December.
Nearly half of the sugar mills in southern Guangxi province, China's main producing area, have ended output for the current season, an official of the Guangxi Sugar and Wine Co said.
The season is expected to end by mid-April.
In Guangxi, ex-factory prices of low-quality sugar stood at about 3,800 yuan per tonne while high-quality sugar stood at 4,300 yuan, another industry official said.
China's total sugar output in the 1996/97 season was forecast at 6.6 million tonnes, a rise of 380,000 tonnes from the previous season, industry officials have said.
